input.question: Why do bands do planned encores at concerts?
input.ground_truth: It’s just tradition at this point. At one point in history encores were real but now every band just does it because it’s the thing every other band does. There are exceptions though, I’ve seen Bad Religion headline numerous times going through a 25-30 song set and just end it with no encore. The Supersuckers announce its time for “the fake encore” about 3 songs from the end...

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do bands do planned encores at concerts?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends are putting on a show for your family. You sing a bunch of songs, and then everyone cheers and claps a lot. But then, your family keeps clapping and shouting, "More! More!" So, you and your friends come back on stage one more time to sing a special song just for them. That extra song at the end is called an "encore." 

Bands do planned encores because the audience really likes them and wants to hear more. Sometimes, the band decides ahead of time which song they will play at the end, so everyone is excited and ready to cheer even louder! It makes the concert extra fun for both the band and the people watching.
